transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-06
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Lena (Redwood AE), Marcus (Redwood SE), Priya (Crescent Head of IT), Tom (Cloud Security Eng), Meera (Compliance)

Summary (auto-generated, may be rough):
Quick discovery focused on security posture and deployment options (hosted vs dedicated vs private). Primary asks: SOC 2 / ISO evidence, SSO/SAML integration, RBAC, audit logs granularity, encryption/KMS model, and data retention / PHI handling. Agreed next steps: share SOC2 docs, schedule architecture deep dive for private/Dedicated, customer to provide retention needs.

Transcript:
[00:00:00] Lena: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, yep we got about 45 minutes, quick intros. I'm Lena, AE at Redwood, Marcus is our SE.
[00:00:12] Priya: Hi all, Priya here, Head of IT at Crescent, joining from Boston. We're evaluating hosted vs dedicated for some patient-facing NLP features, main concerns are compliance and data residency.
[00:00:22] Tom: Tom here, I look after cloud security. I'm particularly interested in how keys are managed, KMS, and audit logs.
[00:00:28] Meera: Meera, compliance — HIPAA and SOC/ISO stuff mainly.
[00:00:33] Marcus: Great, thanks. Quick agenda: we'll run through high-level security posture, answer any questions, and then propose next steps.
[00:00:41] Priya: Sounds good.

[00:01:05] Marcus: To start — Redwood offers hosted API, dedicated reserved capacity, and private (VPC/on-prem). For healthcare you're likely looking at Dedicated or Private given PHI. Hosted can be gated with controls but dedicated gives isolated GPU pools and Private gives you complete VPC control.
[00:01:28] Tom: When you say "private" — do we manage the keys? How does KMS/HSM integration work?
[00:01:36] Marcus: For private deployments you can bring your own KMS or integrate with cloud KMS/HSM. We support AWS KMS / CloudHSM for key wrapping; you hold the master keys in your account if you choose. For Dedicated we offer customer-managed key options via a BYOK flow, or we can manage keys for you with strict contracts.
[00:01:58] Meera: So for encryption at rest and in transit, everything is TLS 1.2+ and storage is encrypted?
[00:02:05] Marcus: Yes TLS in transit, at-rest encryption using AES-256. On private, keys are in your KMS; on hosted we use our KMS but can support customer KMS for enterprise tiers.

[00:02:30] [brief crosstalk]
[00:02:46] Priya: SOC 2 — do you have Type II? And ISO 27001? We need artifacts for our security questionnaire.
[00:02:54] Lena: Yes, we have SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 certifications. I'll share the report and a redacted summary.
[00:03:02] Meera: Great — do you have a controls matrix so we can map to our vendor risk checklist?
[00:03:07] Lena: We do, Marcus will include a controls mapping as well.

[00:03:30] Tom: Audit logs — how granular are they? API-level logs, user-level, token-level? Can we get immutable audit trails with S3 archival?
[00:03:42] Marcus: We provide request-level audit logs that include request metadata, model used, token counts, timestamps, and request IDs. For Dedicated and Private you can forward logs to your SIEM (Splunk/Datadog) or S3 and set retention policies. Hosted customers can have logs exported as part of an enterprise package. We also retain system-level logs for a configurable window.
[00:04:05] Tom: Is there a tamper-evident / append-only audit option?
[00:04:10] Marcus: We support log forwarding to your immutable store; on private deployments you control lifecycle, so you can enforce WORM policies. Hosted is more constrained but we can work on enterprise agreements for longer retention and immutability.

[00:04:38] Priya: SSO — we use SAML 2.0 with Okta. What's the SSO story for the Console and API access?
[00:04:45] Marcus: Console supports SSO via SAML (Okta, OneLogin) and OIDC. RBAC is integrated with SSO so you can map groups to roles. API keys are separate — we recommend short-lived tokens and fine-grained scopes; there is support for token rotation.
[00:05:02] Priya: Can we enforce SCIM provisioning?
[00:05:05] Marcus: Yes SCIM is supported for user provisioning in the Console. For Dedicated/Private you get much more control over authentication connectors.

[00:05:30] Meera: On RBAC — can roles be scoped to model, route, or environment? We want devs to only see dev models, clinicians to access production models, etc.
[00:05:39] Marcus: Roles can be scoped by project and environment and by API route. You can create custom roles — e.g., generate-only vs admin. We'll share our role table. Some of the finer-grained route-level enforcement is part of our enterprise RBAC feature set.

[00:06:15] Tom: Data residency — we need PII and PHI to stay in US-east for now. Does Redwood allow region pinning?
[00:06:23] Marcus: Yes region pinning is possible. Hosted offers region choices for enterprise customers, Dedicated gives you predictable capacity in selected regions, and Private is deployed in your VPC/region.

[00:06:45] Priya: What about data retention and deletion — we need both short-term logs for analytics but also guaranteed deletion after X days for inputs/outputs.
[00:06:55] Marcus: We have configurable retention windows per customer. On hosted some logs are short-lived by default, but enterprise contracts allow custom retention. For Dedicated/Private, you control retention. For deletion we can do configurable TTLs and support on-demand redaction. Note: model caching/prefix cache may store KV cache; on private you manage cache persistence and clearing.

[00:07:25] [15s pause; typing]
[00:07:40] Meera: Do you retain transcript-level content for training? We must ensure no training on PHI.
[00:07:47] Lena: We do not train models on customer data unless there's an explicit opt-in program. We can provide a contractual commitment for healthcare customers.
[00:07:55] Priya: Is there a data processing addendum (DPA) and BAAs for HIPAA?
[00:07:59] Lena: We have a DPA and we can execute a BAA for customers processing PHI — will route legal and security on that.

[00:08:20] Tom: Network controls — for dedicated/private can we use private endpoints, VPC peering, or AWS PrivateLink?
[00:08:27] Marcus: Yes. PrivateLink is supported for hosted enterprise; Dedicated/Private supports VPC peering and private endpoints. We'll share network diagrams and expected firewall rules.

[00:08:50] Priya: On encryption again — are encryption keys ever exported? How is key rotation handled?
[00:08:58] Marcus: For BYOK we never export your master key; we use envelope encryption. Key rotation is supported through KMS practices; if using your KMS you manage rotation. For our managed KMS we rotate according to industry best practices and can provide rotation logs.

[00:09:25] [short filler]
[00:09:38] Meera: Certifications — what version of ISO? Are pen test reports available?
[00:09:43] Lena: ISO 27001 latest scope will be included; we also do yearly pen tests and can share summaries and remediation timelines. Deep pen test reports are available under NDA.

[00:10:05] Tom: For the audit logs, can we include per-request redaction flags so that PHI is not written to certain logs?
[00:10:12] Marcus: We offer redaction hooks; you can configure PII/PHI scrubbing at ingestion or choose not to log payloads. For full production we usually recommend scrubbing or piping raw payloads to your private storage.

[00:10:35] Priya: Latency/cost tradeoff — if we move to dedicated with more isolation do we lose the latest model updates?
[00:10:42] Marcus: Model versions are pinned per deployment; Dedicated can host the model variants you choose. For hosted we update catalog more frequently. Dedicated gives you predictable throughput but you can request model upgrades on rollouts.

[00:11:05] [noise, some crosstalk]
[00:11:20] Meera: One more compliance question — do you provide customer access logs that show who accessed what data and when? We need evidence for audits.
[00:11:28] Marcus: Yes request-level auth logs, user actions in Console, token usage, and admin changes. All can be exported to your SIEM. We'll include sample log schema.

[00:12:02] Priya: Okay that covers most of our list. Next steps?
[00:12:07] Lena: Recap — I'll send SOC2 Type II PDF, ISO summary, and a controls mapping. Marcus will schedule a technical deep dive for private/dedicated networking and KMS integration. Meera/Tom will confirm retention/PHI flow and any specific legal asks.
[00:12:20] Tom: Sounds good. Can we also get an architecture checklist for on-prem/private?
[00:12:26] Marcus: Yep I'll include the checklist and a template VPC diagram.

[00:12:40] Lena: Any blockers on your side for timing?
[00:12:44] Priya: We're on a Q2 timeline, pilot in April if security answers are good.
[00:12:49] Lena: Great, we'll prioritize docs this week.

[00:13:05] [wrap up small talk]
[00:13:30] Meera: Thanks — please include any specific attestations about not using data for training.
[00:13:36] Lena: Will do, will include contractual language and DPA/BAA draft.

[00:13:48] Lena: Thanks all, meeting notes and action items will be sent.

[END OF TRANSCRIPT]
